landscape.title: Founder programmes an early-stage Indian founder is likely to compare
landscape.release: Compiled by hand from each programme's public pages

programmes.name: Razorpay Rize
programmes.leadOffer: Company registration, founder communities and YC application help
programmes.detail: Registration for Pvt Ltd, LLP and OPC. Three communities: Tech+, D2C+, Xport+. Rize for YC (application reviews, mock interviews), Pitch Perfect, Razorpay Ventures.
programmes.entryBar: Open to early-stage founders in India

programmes.name: Stripe Atlas
programmes.detail: Delaware C corporation or LLC, tax ID, founder equity paperwork, $2,500 in Stripe credits. US$100 a year after the first year.
programmes.entryBar: Anyone, including founders outside the US

programmes.name: AWS Activate
programmes.detail: Founders tier: starts at $1,000, up to $5,000, for self-funded startups. Portfolio tier: up to $200,000, needs an ID from an accelerator, investor or other Activate Provider.
programmes.entryBar: Low for the small tier; a backer for the large one
programmes.meetsFounder: After there is a product to host

programmes.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program
programmes.detail: Reported as up to $2,000 for unfunded startups and up to $200,000 over two years for startups with institutional funding.
programmes.entryBar: Low for the small tier; institutional funding for the large one
programmes.meetsFounder: After there is a product to host

programmes.name: Microsoft for Startups
programmes.detail: Open to private companies building a software product; no investor needed to join. Larger credit tiers are reported to need funding, customers or an accelerator.
programmes.entryBar: Low to join; traction for larger tiers
programmes.meetsFounder: After there is a product to host
programmes.verified: official page for eligibility; secondary sources for tiers

programmes.name: Zoho for Startups
programmes.detail: Reported as ₹1 lakh on approval plus ₹86,000 for hosting email with Zoho; up to ₹3 lakh for DPIIT-recognised startups. For new Zoho users only.
programmes.entryBar: DPIIT recognition or a partner incubator
programmes.verified: secondary sources, including the Startup India partner page

read: Four of the six lead with credits. Credits are easy to compare and easy to match, so those programmes compete on the size of the number.
Rize and Stripe Atlas are the two that meet a founder before the company exists, and both are run by payments companies. Atlas forms US companies; Rize forms Indian ones.
Both Rize and Atlas use company formation to meet founders early. They sit on opposite sides of the choice many YC-bound Indian founders face: an Indian company or a US one.

decisions.title: 12 of the 20 YC companies on Rize's alumni wall are listed as US companies
decisions.recommendation: Public counts of "Indian startups in YC" are counts of locations, and most of the companies Rize names as alumni aren't in them. If Rize wants to show what Rize for YC contributes, the directory can't do it, but Rize's own records can. A per-batch count of Rize-supported and Indian-founder YC companies is a number only Rize can publish.

metric.label: Rize alumni by where YC lists them
metric.comparison: 20 companies is below the minimum sample of 30, so no percentage is stated

evidence: Rize's public Rize for YC page names 20 YC companies. All 20 were found in the YC directory, and for 20 of them the founder Rize names appears on the company's own YC page.
Directory, 2023–2026: 26 companies list India. 6 of those are on Rize's wall.

Another 13 companies on the wall from the same batches are listed under another country or none. Counting those, at least 39 YC companies in 2023–2026 have a link to India's founder ecosystem, not 26.
This is a YC-wide shift, not something particular to Rize: across all of YC, the share of companies listing San Francisco rose from 32% (2019–2022) to 61% (2023–2026).
Over the same period the directory's India share fell from 7.6% to 1.1%. Some of that fall is this change in where companies list themselves; how much can't be measured from outside.
decisions.counterEvidence: Being on the wall means a company used Rize's application help; it doesn't show that Rize is why it got in. The wall shows companies Rize chose to feature, so it isn't every founder Rize supported. Companies in a current batch may list San Francisco only while the batch runs. The page's headline says 18 founders while it names 20 companies.
decisions.source: razorpay.com/rize/ycombinator + yc-oss YC directory + ycombinator.com company pages

decisions.title: Karnataka supplies most of India's listed YC companies
decisions.recommendation: Report Rize for YC admits by the founder's home state, not the company's listed city. Admits from outside Karnataka are the ones Rize can most credibly claim, and only Rize's application data can show them.

metric.label: Karnataka's share of India-listed YC admits, 2019–2023

evidence: Karnataka: 98 admits from 10,874 recognised startups (9.01 per 1,000 vs 0.79 elsewhere).
All 7 India-listed Rize alumni are in Karnataka.
decisions.counterEvidence: Much of this is relocation: founders from other states move to Bengaluru and list it as their location. The directory can't show where a founder started.
decisions.source: yc-oss YC directory + DPIIT recognitions (PIB, Feb 2024)

decisions.title: Gujarat: worth a small Rize for YC pilot, not a conclusion
decisions.recommendation: Gujarat is growing fast in registered startups but almost never appears in YC. The likely reason is sector mix, not missed outreach. A cheap test would settle it: one application clinic there, measured on qualified applications.

metric.label: Gujarat: YC admits per 1,000 recognised startups

evidence: Gujarat: 1 YC admit(s) from 8,619 recognised startups in 2019–2023; recognitions grew 5.8× (India 3.3×).
Gap must be at least 1.5× and pass a Holm-corrected noise screen across 32 states.
decisions.counterEvidence: DPIIT recognition covers every kind of new business. A state heavy in manufacturing, trading or services will send few companies to YC whatever Rize does. This compares two different lists of companies, so it is not a conversion rate.
decisions.source: yc-oss YC directory + DPIIT recognitions (PIB, Feb 2024)

decisions.title: Startup registrations are growing fastest outside the big hubs
decisions.recommendation: Registrations grew well above India's 3.3× in Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu, and well below it in Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Karnataka and Kerala. Before moving any events budget, check whether Rize's own sign-ups show the same shift. The "Try it on your data" screen does that comparison.
evidence: These are complete government counts, so sampling error is not the concern. A state is listed only if its gap exceeds 5 percentage points and passes a Holm-corrected noise screen across 23 states.
decisions.counterEvidence: DPIIT recognition is opt-in. Several states tie local benefits to it, so a jump can mean a registration drive, not more founders. Company-incorporation counts would be the right cross-check; the free MCA data was not reachable for this build.

withheld.title: India's true share of YC: not called
reason: The directory shows India's share falling from 7.6% to 1.1%, but it records where a company says it is, not where its founders are from. 12 of 20 Rize alumni are filed under the USA, and across all of YC the share listing San Francisco rose from 32% to 61%. So the fall in Indian-founder companies is smaller than the directory shows, by an amount public data can't measure.
withheld.whatWouldSettleIt: A count of Indian-founder companies per YC batch. Rize for YC's application records are the closest thing to one.

withheld.title: Closure rates by state: not called
reason: Gujarat's closure rate (3.0% vs 4.7% elsewhere) looks different, but Gujarat is also one of the fastest-growing states. Younger startups have had less time to close, so state totals can't separate a healthier ecosystem from a younger one.
Karnataka (5.6% vs 4.4%) is under the 1.5× size bar, so it isn't worth acting on.
Tamil Nadu (3.7% vs 4.6%) is under the 1.5× size bar, so it isn't worth acting on.
withheld.whatWouldSettleIt: Closures broken down by year of recognition for each state, so startups of the same age can be compared.

withheld.title: Survival of recent YC companies: too new to call
reason: 2024 (n=7), 2025 (n=3), 2026 (n=6): fewer than 3 years old and below the minimum sample of 30. All 20 Rize alumni are still active, but 14 of them are from these batches, so that says little yet.
withheld.whatWouldSettleIt: Time. These cohorts become readable once they are 3 years old.
